prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK’s 2024 Contract (policies and figures only)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration and stop small boats.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; reduce household energy costs.
- Expand domestic energy supply; scrap Net Zero policies.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential immigration (healthcare as key exception).
- Create a Department of Immigration; leave ECHR for removals policy.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals (offshore if needed); bar asylum from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens; deport foreign offenders after sentences.
- Bar student dependents; tighten rules so only students with essential skills can remain.
- Five-year residency and employment requirement to claim benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise employers’ NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt health/care and firms ≤5 staff). Claimed: £5–10bn savings p.a.; £4bn revenue p.a.

Government spending and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (claimed £35bn p.a. saving).
- Departmental efficiency target: save £5 in every £100 (claimed £50bn p.a.).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (claimed £6bn p.a.); reduce retained EU/other regulations; improve HMRC tax collection. Total “waste” savings claimed: £91bn p.a.

Personal taxation and cost of living
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT and environmental levies on energy.
- Stamp Duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% over £1.5m.
- Abolish VAT “tourist tax”; abolish Inheritance Tax below £2m (20% above). Claimed cost: £70bn p.a.

Business and growth
- No corporation tax for profits up to £100k; main rate cut to 20% then 15% (year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Later: abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; planning reform; simplify employment/tax rules. Claimed cost: £18bn p.a.

NHS and social care
- Zero basic rate income tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; student fee write-off tied to service.
- Use independent/overseas capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Vouchers if GP wait >3 days, consultant >3 weeks, operation >9 weeks.
- Operational reforms; Pharmacy First campaign; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms. Claimed cost: £17bn p.a.

Energy and Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero targets and renewable subsidies (replace via equivalent taxes).
- Fast‑track North Sea oil/gas and shale test sites; expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies. Claimed saving: £30bn p.a.

Law, order, and justice
- Recruit 40,000 police over 5 years; increase stop and search; revise recruitment/standards; reduce non-operational roles. Claimed cost: £3bn p.a.
- Automatic life sentences for violent repeat offenders; increase justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; 10,000 extra prison places; revise hate crime definition. Claimed cost: £2bn p.a.

Education and families
- Revise curriculum to require balanced teaching on imperialism/slavery.
- Restrict gender identity policies in schools; parental notification; single‑sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; stricter university entry; expand PRUs; optional 2‑year degrees. Claimed cost: £5bn p.a.
- Family measures: transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front‑load Child Benefit ages 1–4; smartphone safeguards. Claimed cost: £8bn p.a.

Housing
- Fast‑track brownfield development; prioritize locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold reforms. Cost neutral (claimed).

Transport and infrastructure
- Scrap remaining HS2 (claimed £25bn one-off saving).
- Ban ULEZ/Clean Air Zones and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods; no ICE car bans.
- Regional transport upgrades; new 50% public/50% UK pension‑fund utility model; cap standing charges; single infrastructure funding stream. Claimed saving: £5bn p.a. (plus £25bn one‑off).

Agriculture and fisheries
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate‑linked subsidies; reduce red tape; support “Buy British.” Claimed cost: £2bn p.a.
- Tighten access to UK waters; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing/fleet. Claimed cost: £2bn p.a.

Defence and veterans
- Spend 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; new justice bill; dedicated veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement/industry reforms. Claimed cost: £14bn p.a.

Brexit and constitutional
- Scrap retained EU laws; abandon Windsor Framework; consider TCA renegotiation.
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act, House of Lords, civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights. Cost neutral (claimed).

Reclaiming Britain
- Oppose WHO treaty/CBDC; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; reform BBC/licence fee; new anti‑corruption unit; new public holidays. Cost neutral (claimed).

Overall funding (party’s figures)
- Claimed annual savings: £150bn; additional tax from growth: £10bn; total £160bn.
- Claimed annual costs: £141bn.
